Lessons.Title: Use the Four Operations to Solve Problems
ExplanationParagraphs: Warm-up original True or False:2×40=2×4×10 TRUE,2×40=8×10 TRUE,3×50=15×10 TRUE,3×40=7×10 FALSE because left120 vs right70. Show why using groups of ten, not only final values.

Activity1 original situation: 142 guests at party, roomA has94, roomB six equal tables,4 pieces of silverware and1 plate per guest. Source prompts pupils to propose their OWN mathematical questions; not every possible question has a publisher fixed answer. Teacher highlights 'How many guests at each roomB table?': roomB142−94=48, then48÷6=8. A combined expression (142−94)÷6=g shows which operation comes first. Equivalent relation (g×6)+94=142 is acknowledged.

Independently proposed, not publisher-fixed focus questions from source data include142×4=568 pieces of silverware and142 plates if one per guest; these may be checked as scalar skill examples but are not substituted for the source open-question activity.

Activity2 Party Problems has three original two-step stories: Kiran has156 paper rings through Thursday, and Friday Kiran PLUS TWO friends each makes9:156+(3×9)=183 rings. Mai has168 muffins, puts104 in basket and shares64 remaining across8 boxes:(168−104)÷8=8 muffins each.184 cups on table, three tables of8 each take one cup:184−(3×8)=160 cups remaining.

Teacher checks each written equation contains a letter for unknown and parenthesis to reflect first operation; teach MLR5 Co-Craft Questions and oral explanation. Original student section summary4×30=120,7×13=91,3×28=84 appears with base-ten/area diagrams.

Five original source visual assets inspected locally; publisher paper party decoration and original asset pixels not copied. Protected Andre's Balloons Cool-down and student task PDF not verified. Authored tests unrun, Stage D and academic review pending.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two-step equation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Represent two sequential operations and their appropriate order.

KeyConcepts.Title: Unknown symbol
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use a letter for target quantity in a contextual equation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Combined operations
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use add/subtract/multiply/divide as the story requires.
